Adonikam
ad-oh-NYE-kam
proper noun
Hebrew Adoniqam (H140), my Lord has arisen — from adon (H113), lord, master, and qum (H6965), to rise, to stand up.

Biblical Definition

Adonikam heads one of the lay families of the return from Babylon. Ezra's register numbers his children six hundred sixty and six (Ezr 2:13) and Nehemiah's six hundred threescore and seven (Neh 7:18); and like several houses, a later company came up with Ezra himself — of the last sons of Adonikam, whose names are these, Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah, and with them threescore males (Ezr 8:13). The phrase the last sons is worth noticing: the register is careful to mark that these came afterward, the stragglers of the house, and it gives their three names individually rather than lumping them in. The name itself is a resurrection sentence: my Lord has arisen. That such a confession should head a family carried captive to Babylon, whose sons trickled home over two generations, is the shape of the whole restoration. The LORD had said through Jeremiah that after seventy years He would visit them and perform His good word; the return was His rising to do it. The Christian reads the name further still, to the morning when the word was spoken plainly: He is not here: for he is risen, as he said (Mat 28:6).

Origin & Era

Head of a lay family of the return from Babylon, whose last sons came up later with Ezra; the name means my Lord has arisen.

ADONIKAM, Hebrew Adoniqam, my Lord has arisen.

The head of one of the families that returned from the Babylonian captivity.

Six hundred sixty and six of his children returned with Zerubbabel.

Eliphelet, Jeiel and Shemaiah, the last sons of Adonikam, came up later with Ezra.

Threescore males came up with them.

Key Scripture

Ezr 2:13 — "The children of Adonikam, six hundred sixty and six."

Ezr 8:13 — "And of the last sons of Adonikam, whose names are these, Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah, and with them threescore males."

Neh 7:18 — "The children of Adonikam, six hundred threescore and seven."

Mat 28:6 — "He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay."

Modern Corruption

The number six hundred sixty and six is read as an occult signature wherever it appears; here it is a plain count of a family coming home.

expand to see more

Ezra 2:13 is a small trap for a certain kind of reader. The number of Adonikam's children is six hundred sixty and six, and the association with Revelation 13:18 is instant and, in this case, entirely groundless. Nehemiah's parallel register gives six hundred sixty and seven for the same house, which by itself should settle the matter: the figures are two counts taken at different times, not a cipher. Scripture uses numbers as numbers far more often than as symbols, and a reader who cannot tell a census total from an apocalyptic sign will find portents everywhere and doctrine nowhere.

The discipline this requires is the ordinary one of reading each text according to its kind. Revelation is a book of signs and says so; Ezra 2 is a register and says so. Rightly dividing the word of truth (2Ti 2:15) includes knowing what sort of writing is in front of you. The principle to recover is sobriety in interpretation: the Bible is not a code to be cracked by the ingenious but a revelation to be received by the humble, and the number of Adonikam's household is the number of Adonikam's household.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Adoniqam (H140), from adon (H113), lord, and qum (H6965), to arise.

expand to see more

Hebrew adon (H113) — lord, master, owner; the common Hebrew title of authority.

Hebrew qum (H6965) — to arise, stand, be established; Arise, O LORD; save me, O my God (Psa 3:7).

Hebrew Adoniqam (H140) — head of a returning family, Ezra 2:13, 8:13, Nehemiah 7:18.

Hebrew acharon (H314) — last, latter; the last sons of Adonikam (Ezr 8:13).

Greek egeiro (G1453) — to raise up, to rise; he is risen, as he said (Mat 28:6).

Usage

"“The children of Adonikam, six hundred sixty and six”."

"“The last sons of Adonikam, whose names are these”."

"“The children of Adonikam, six hundred threescore and seven” — Nehemiah's count."
